options.content: A small text file that lets a website recognise a user
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: A program that runs on the computer to speed up browsing
options.rationale: A cookie is data, not a program.

options.content: A virus that spreads from website to website
options.rationale: Cookies cannot run, so they are not viruses.

options.content: A list of web addresses the user has saved
options.rationale: That describes bookmarks.

explanation: A cookie is a small text file sent by a web server, stored by the browser and sent back on later requests.

options.content: When the browser is closed
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: When the computer's hard drive is full
options.rationale: Session cookies do not depend on storage space.

options.content: After exactly one year
options.rationale: Expiry dates apply to persistent cookies.

options.content: Only when the user deletes it
options.rationale: Session cookies are removed automatically.

explanation: Session cookies are held in temporary memory and deleted when the browser closes; persistent cookies remain until they expire or are deleted.

stem: A news website shows its pages in English every time Tatenda visits, because he chose English a month ago. What kind of cookie stores this choice?

options.content: Session cookie
options.rationale: A session cookie would be deleted when the browser closed.

options.content: Shopping basket cookie
options.rationale: There is no such separate type; baskets use session cookies.

options.content: Encryption cookie
options.rationale: No such cookie type exists in the syllabus.

options.content: Persistent cookie
options.rationale: Correct: it lasts between visits.

explanation: Preferences remembered between visits need a persistent cookie.

options.content: On the website's web server only
options.rationale: The server sends the cookie; the browser keeps it.

options.content: On the user's device, by the web browser
options.rationale: Correct: the browser stores it and sends it back to the site.

options.content: On the DNS server
options.rationale: DNS servers hold domain names and IP addresses.

options.content: In the router of the user's network
options.rationale: Routers forward packets; they do not store cookies.

explanation: The web server sends the cookie; the browser stores it on the user's device and returns it with later requests.

stem: Which is the best example of a use for a **session** cookie?

options.content: Remembering a user's login for next month
options.rationale: That needs a persistent cookie.

options.content: Keeping items in a shopping basket while the user browses
options.rationale: Correct: needed only during the visit.

options.content: Remembering a chosen language for future visits
options.rationale: That needs a persistent cookie.

options.content: Building a record of interests over many weeks
options.rationale: Long-term tracking uses persistent cookies.

explanation: Session cookies support one visit, such as keeping a basket or a login while moving between pages.

stem: Why can persistent cookies be a privacy risk on a computer in an internet café?

options.content: Cookies can delete files on the café's computers
options.rationale: Cookies are text files and cannot delete anything.

options.content: Cookies slow the café's internet connection
options.rationale: Cookies are tiny; they do not noticeably slow connections.

options.content: Cookies stop the browser from using HTTPS
options.rationale: Cookies have no effect on HTTPS.

options.content: The next user may enter the last user's account
options.rationale: Correct: a stored login cookie lets the site recognise the computer, not the person.

explanation: A persistent login cookie stays on the shared computer, so the website may treat the next user as the previous one. Users should log out, avoid "remember me" and use private browsing.
hints: What does a "remember me" cookie do when someone else uses the same browser?

stem: Rudo notices adverts for school shoes on many different websites after looking at shoes on one shop's site. Which explains this?

options.content: A session cookie copied itself to the other websites
options.rationale: Cookies cannot copy themselves; they are data.

options.content: The DNS server sold her browsing history to shops
options.rationale: DNS servers translate names; they do not deliver adverts.

options.content: An advertiser's third-party cookies tracked her
options.rationale: Correct: the same advertiser's cookie is read on every site showing its adverts.

options.content: Her browser's bookmarks were sent to every website
options.rationale: Browsers do not send bookmarks to websites.

explanation: An advertising company sets a third-party cookie when its advert appears on the shoe shop's page; when its adverts appear on other sites, the same cookie is sent back, so it knows her interests.
hints: Who places the adverts on all those different websites?

stem: A persistent cookie remains on the device after the browser is closed.
explanation: True. It stays until its expiry date or until the user deletes it.

stem: A cookie can run on a computer and infect it like a virus.
explanation: False. A cookie is a small text file of data and cannot run.

stem: Match each use to the type of cookie most likely to be used.

left.content: Items kept in a basket during one shopping visit
A chosen dark display mode kept for next week
Staying logged in while moving between pages of one visit

explanation: Needed only during one visit: session cookie. Needed on later visits: persistent cookie.

stem: Name the type of cookie that is held in temporary memory and deleted when the browser closes.
explanation: Session cookies last for one browsing session only.

stem: Describe **four** ways in which websites use cookies. [4]

points.description: Saving personal details (e.g. name, address) to fill forms
Holding items in an online shopping basket
Storing login details so the user stays logged in (or tracking browsing for targeted adverts)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Cookies save personal details such as a delivery address, remember preferences such as language, keep items in a shopping basket while the user browses, and store login details so the user need not sign in again.

explanation: Personal details, preferences, shopping baskets, login details (and tracking for adverts).
hints: Think of an online shop: what does it need to remember?

stem: Evaluate the use of persistent cookies for a user of a social media site. [3]

points.description: Benefit: stays logged in / preferences remembered, saving time
Drawback: browsing can be tracked and a profile built (privacy) / risk on shared computers
Management: the user can delete or block cookies, log out or use private browsing

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Persistent cookies save time because the user stays logged in and preferences are kept. However, they allow the site and advertisers to track browsing and build a profile, and on a shared computer another person could access the account. Deleting cookies or logging out reduces the risk.

explanation: Convenience versus privacy, with ways to manage cookies.
hints: Give a benefit, a drawback, and a way to reduce the drawback.

stem: An online pharmacy in Bulawayo uses cookies on its website.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe the difference between a session cookie and a persistent cookie.

points.description: A session cookie is stored in temporary memory and deleted when the browser is closed
A persistent cookie is saved on the device and remains until its expiry date or until deleted

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A session cookie is deleted when the browser closes, whereas a persistent cookie stays on the device until it expires or is deleted.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Which cookie keeps a customer's basket while they move between pages?

options.content: Persistent cookie
options.rationale: Not needed after the visit.

options.content: Third-party cookie
options.rationale: Third-party cookies come from other domains, e.g. advertisers.

options.content: Session cookie
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Tracking cookie
options.rationale: Tracking is for adverts, not baskets.

parts.explanation: Basket during one visit: session cookie.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain **one** privacy concern that customers may have about the pharmacy's cookies.

points.description: Cookies can record what products / pages a customer views
which could reveal sensitive health information or be used for targeted adverts / shared with third parties

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Cookies can record which medicines a customer looks at, revealing private health information that could be used for adverts or shared with other companies.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State **one** way a customer can manage cookies in a browser.

points.description: Delete cookies / block third-party cookies / use private browsing / decline non-essential cookies

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Delete stored cookies in the browser settings.

explanation: Session versus persistent; privacy; managing cookies.
hints: Session: one visit. Persistent: between visits.
Name a privacy risk and a way to manage it.

stem: Farai visits an online music shop for the first time and chooses to view prices in US dollars.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe how a cookie lets the shop show prices in US dollars when Farai returns next week.

points.description: The web server sends a cookie holding the currency choice (and an identifier) to Farai's browser
The browser stores it on his device as a persistent cookie
When Farai visits again, the browser sends the cookie back with the request
The server reads it and shows the prices in US dollars

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The server sends a persistent cookie containing his currency choice; the browser stores it; next week the browser sends it back with the request, and the server reads it and displays prices in US dollars.

parts.stem: Which statement about this cookie is correct?

options.content: It is a program that changes prices
options.rationale: Cookies are data, not programs.

options.content: It is stored only on the web server
options.rationale: The browser stores it.

options.content: It is a small text file of data
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: It is deleted when the browser closes
options.rationale: That would be a session cookie.

explanation: Persistent cookie: stored by the browser, returned on the next visit.
